set.body:
Problem:
File-producing pipelines are first-class Sojourn use cases, but TaskOutcome.Succeeded currently exposes only the structured RemoteRef and the Slurm adapter constructs an empty declared-output contract. scala-slurm can validate path, size, and digest, yet Sojourn discards that manifest and publishes no durable artifact references.

Ownership:
- Sojourn owns scheduler-neutral artifact declarations, durable references, publication semantics, and pipeline composition.
- scala-slurm owns sandbox-relative output staging, sealing, digest verification, epoch fencing, and verified attachment.
- The sojourn-slurm adapter lowers declarations and imports verified outputs without exposing absolute compute-node paths.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sojourn core defines validated relative artifact paths, declarations, metadata, durable artifact references, and an immutable artifact set without depending on scala-slurm.
- SiteOperation can declare outputs, and TaskOutcome success carries the structured result plus the complete durable artifact set.
- Existing value-only operations remain source-compatible through empty-output defaults or documented migration helpers.
- The local backend and Slurm backend implement identical artifact outcome semantics.
- The Slurm adapter lowers Sojourn declarations to scala-slurm declared outputs and never passes an empty observed-output vector when outputs were declared.
- Every promoted artifact is checked against the worker-sealed size and digest while entering SiteStore; an absolute worker path is never part of portable identity.
- Success is published only after all declared artifacts are durable; partial imports cannot appear as a successful artifact set.
- Publication failure is typed separately from workload failure and retains verified workload/result evidence for recovery without blind re-execution.
- Tests cover nested paths, duplicates, traversal rejection, empty outputs, multi-artifact success, missing/extra/corrupt output, partial publication failure, deduplication, local/Slurm parity, and stored-artifact reuse as downstream input.
- Architecture and migration docs state the ownership boundary and lifecycle.
- Focused suites and the full Sojourn gate pass; affected scala-slurm result/worker suites remain green.
set.title: SCOMP.6: Promote declared task files into durable Sojourn artifacts
